WITH dedup_messages AS ( -- agent_messages is a ReplacingMergeTree(ingested_at) ORDER BY (session_id, -- litellm_call_id) - a reparse job that re-INSERTs a corrected row (rather -- than replacing in place) leaves both the old and new row physically -- present until a background merge (or an explicit FINAL/OPTIMIZE) collapses -- them; a plain equality JOIN against the raw table sees BOTH rows and -- silently double-renders (or even triples/quadruples) every prompt/reply -- line for that call - reproduced live against this very dashboard's own -- session trace, not just the reported Codex/chatgpt sessions, since -- agent_messages accumulates un-merged duplicate rows broadly whenever -- ingestion runs more than once for the same litellm_call_id. Same root -- cause and same fix pattern as child_anchor's own dedup of -- agent_invocations above (also a ReplacingMergeTree with no FINAL applied -- here) - argMax by ingested_at picks the single latest-ingested row per -- (session_id, litellm_call_id), mirroring what the table's own version -- column would resolve to once merged. SELECT m2.session_id AS session_id, m2.litellm_call_id AS litellm_call_id, argMax(m2.prompt_text, m2.ingested_at) AS prompt_text, argMax(m2.response_text, m2.ingested_at) AS response_text FROM agent_messages m2 WHERE m2.litellm_call_id != '' AND (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], m2.session_id)) GROUP BY m2.session_id, m2.litellm_call_id ), scoped_events AS ( SELECT ev.session_id AS session_id, ev.timestamp AS timestamp, ev.tool_name AS tool_name, ev.litellm_call_id AS litellm_call_id, ev.agent_invocation_id AS agent_invocation_id, ev.command_name AS command_name, ev.status AS status, ev.latency_ms AS latency_ms, ev.calculated_type AS calculated_type, ev.calculated_payload AS calculated_payload, ev.failed_tool_name AS failed_tool_name, ev.failed_tool_error AS failed_tool_error, m.prompt_text AS prompt_text, m.response_text AS response_text, -- Bug fix: dedup must catch a prompt_text reappearing anywhere earlier in -- this same (session_id, agent_invocation_id), not merely on the -- immediately-preceding row - a lagInFrame-based "differs from the row -- right before it" check misses the case where an unrelated row (a -- system_notification, a suggestion_mode prompt, ...) is sandwiched -- between two calls that both still carry the same underlying real user -- message in context, which let that message re-render as a spurious -- duplicate ❯ marker further down the trace. min(timestamp) OVER a -- partition keyed on the exact prompt_text itself (no ORDER BY, so the -- frame is the whole partition) gives the timestamp of that text's FIRST -- occurrence anywhere in this agent_invocation_id; a row is the one that -- should render as a marker iff its own timestamp equals that minimum, -- i.e. it IS the first occurrence - exactly the "was this exact -- prompt_text already shown at any earlier point" check needed, not just -- "differs from my immediate predecessor". min(ev.timestamp) OVER ( PARTITION BY ev.session_id, ev.agent_invocation_id, m.prompt_text ) AS first_prompt_occurrence_ts, -- Bug fix (4th "Prompts:" inflation bug): a prompt_kind='command' row's -- RAW prompt_text can legitimately change between Codex's own repeated -- self-resends of the SAME command invocation, because harness wrappers -- like embed a live, changing -- token-budget counter ("Tokens used: N") inside the raw text itself - -- confirmed against real session 019f9b12-411f-7193-b498-28f5367df9a8, -- where the same /goal continuation was auto-resent by Codex (no new -- human input) with prompt_text lengths 5400 then 5404 (4 extra digits -- from the counter), defeating first_prompt_occurrence_ts's byte-exact -- dedup above and counting one ongoing /goal prompt as multiple. The -- ingest-computed display_text (calculated_payload) is already stripped -- of this noise for command-kind rows (see _prompt_kind_and_display in -- services/_common/src/ingest_parsing.py) - two command rows with the same command_name + -- display_text are the same underlying prompt, just resent, so dedup -- them on that clean key instead of raw prompt_text. Only used for -- prompt_kind='command' rows (selected via effective_first_prompt_ts in -- prompt_calc below) - real/freeform human prompts keep the existing -- byte-exact dedup unchanged, since they don't have this changing- -- counter problem. min(ev.timestamp) OVER ( PARTITION BY ev.session_id, ev.agent_invocation_id, ev.command_name, JSONExtractString(ev.calculated_payload, 'display_text') ) AS first_command_occurrence_ts, -- A newly-spawned subagent's own conversation begins with a "user"-role -- message that is actually the task/prompt the orchestrator's model -- handed it via the Agent tool_use's own arguments - not anything a -- human typed. Every subsequent turn inside that subagent still resolves -- to this same text as its "last human-originated" turn (no further -- genuine human input ever arrives mid-subagent), so it only survives -- prompt_calc's dedup once, on the very first row of the invocation. -- row_number()=1 within (session_id, agent_invocation_id) identifies -- that first row, used below (is_agent_task) to render it with the -- assistant-text marker/style instead of the real-user-prompt ❯ marker. row_number() OVER ( PARTITION BY ev.session_id, ev.agent_invocation_id ORDER BY ev.timestamp ) AS rn_in_invocation, -- MERGED (scoped_events perf collapse): plan_proposals_match/tool_render/ -- reply_trunc/reply_render/failure_error used to be 5 separate CTEs, each -- a pure per-row projection (or a same-key ASOF join) with no GROUP BY/ -- aggregation of its own, keyed entirely off columns already on this row -- - yet each was referenced as its own CTE built on top of scoped_events, -- and ClickHouse re-executes a WITH-CTE's full definition on every -- textual reference to it (see the clickhouse-sql skill's GOTCHAS.md, -- "CTE re-execution multiplication"). scoped_events alone measured -- ~136ms/20,680 rows per execution and was referenced ~8 times directly, -- plus once more via each of these five downstream CTEs - folding them -- into extra columns computed once, right here, removes that redundant -- re-scanning entirely. Same "MERGED" technique already used further -- below for prompt_final's own 3-way UNION ALL collapse. Each column's -- guard condition is an exact copy of that former CTE's own WHERE clause, -- so a row that wouldn't have produced a matching CTE row still gets NULL -- here, preserving the exact LEFT/INNER JOIN-miss semantics downstream. -- plan_proposals_match: was its own CTE ASOF-joining plan_proposals onto -- scoped_events (WHERE tool_name = 'ExitPlanMode'), then re-joined back -- onto scoped_events by litellm_call_id inside tool_render - a round -- trip that always lands back on this exact same row (litellm_call_id is -- unique per row). Doing the ASOF join directly here instead, for every -- row unconditionally (a cheap merge-sorted lookup), gives the identical -- nearest-preceding plan_text; only the ExitPlanMode branch below ever -- reads it. pp.plan_text AS plan_text, -- tool_render columns: identical expressions to the former tool_render -- CTE, gated by the exact same WHERE condition that CTE used. if(ev.tool_name != '' AND ev.tool_name != 'Agent' AND ev.status != 'failure' AND ev.calculated_type IN ('tool_call', 'skill_call'), if(ev.tool_name IN ('AskUserQuestion', 'ExitPlanMode'), '', substringUTF8(replaceRegexpAll(JSONExtractString(ev.calculated_payload, 'tool_display_arg'), '[ \t\n\r]+', ' '), 1, 110) ), NULL ) AS raw_args, if(raw_args IS NOT NULL, replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll(raw_args, '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>'), NULL ) AS escaped_args, if(ev.tool_name != '' AND ev.tool_name != 'Agent' AND ev.status != 'failure' AND ev.calculated_type IN ('tool_call', 'skill_call'), if(ev.tool_name = 'AskUserQuestion', '', if(ev.tool_name = 'ExitPlanMode', replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll( coalesce(pp.plan_text, ''), '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>'), '"', '"'), replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll( replaceRegexpAll(JSONExtractString(ev.calculated_payload, 'tool_display_arg'), '[ \t\n\r]+', ' '), '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>'), '"', '"') ) ), NULL ) AS full_args_attr, -- reply_trunc (trunc): identical expression/WHERE to the former -- reply_trunc CTE (shared by both the plain-reply branch and the -- tool_name != '' "commentary" branch further below - see that former -- CTE's own comment for why its WHERE was intentionally broader than -- reply_render's own). if(trimBoth(coalesce(m.response_text, '')) != '', multiIf( lengthUTF8(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(m.response_text, '[ \t]+', ' '), '\n{2,}', '\n')) <= 1500, replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(m.response_text, '[ \t]+', ' '), '\n{2,}', '\n'), concat( trimRight( if( extractGroups(substringUTF8(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(m.response_text, '[ \t]+', ' '), '\n{2,}', '\n'), 1, 1500), '(?s)^(.*)[ \t\n]')[1] != '', extractGroups(substringUTF8(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(m.response_text, '[ \t]+', ' '), '\n{2,}', '\n'), 1, 1500), '(?s)^(.*)[ \t\n]')[1], substringUTF8(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(m.response_text, '[ \t]+', ' '), '\n{2,}', '\n'), 1, 1500) ) ), '...' ) ), NULL ) AS trunc, -- reply_render columns (is_webpage/styled_no_br/is_multiline/ -- last_line_len): identical expressions/WHERE to the former reply_render -- CTE, reusing the `trunc` column computed just above instead of a -- separate join (same reply_render-internal 3x expression repetition as -- before - a separately-flagged, out-of-scope cleanup, not touched here). if(ev.tool_name = '' AND ev.status != 'failure' AND trimBoth(coalesce(m.response_text, '')) != '', startsWith(m.response_text, 'Web page content'), NULL ) AS is_webpage, if(ev.tool_name = '' AND ev.status != 'failure' AND trimBoth(coalesce(m.response_text, '')) != '', replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll( if(startsWith(m.response_text, 'Web page content'), concat(substringUTF8(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(m.response_text, '[ \t]+', ' '), '\n{2,}', '\n'), 1, 120), '...'), trunc ), '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>' ), '\*\*([^*\n]+?)\*\*', '\1'), '(?s)```([a-zA-Z0-9+_-]*)\n(.*?)```', '\2'), '`([^`\n]+?)`', '\1'), '(?m)^(#{1,3}) (.*?)$', '\2'), NULL ) AS styled_no_br, if(ev.tool_name = '' AND ev.status != 'failure' AND trimBoth(coalesce(m.response_text, '')) != '', position(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll( if(startsWith(m.response_text, 'Web page content'), concat(substringUTF8(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(m.response_text, '[ \t]+', ' '), '\n{2,}', '\n'), 1, 120), '...'), trunc ), '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>' ), '\*\*([^*\n]+?)\*\*', '\1'), '(?s)```([a-zA-Z0-9+_-]*)\n(.*?)```', '\2'), '`([^`\n]+?)`', '\1'), '(?m)^(#{1,3}) (.*?)$', '\2'), '\n') > 0, NULL ) AS is_multiline, if(ev.tool_name = '' AND ev.status != 'failure' AND trimBoth(coalesce(m.response_text, '')) != '', lengthUTF8( replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll( replaceRegexpAll( arrayElement(splitByChar('\n', assumeNotNull(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll( if(startsWith(m.response_text, 'Web page content'), concat(substringUTF8(replaceRegexpAll(replaceRegexpAll(m.response_text, '[ \t]+', ' '), '\n{2,}', '\n'), 1, 120), '...'), trunc ), '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>' ), '\*\*([^*\n]+?)\*\*', '\1'), '(?s)```([a-zA-Z0-9+_-]*)\n(.*?)```', '\2'), '`([^`\n]+?)`', '\1'), '(?m)^(#{1,3}) (.*?)$', '\2'))), -1), '<[^>]+>', '' ), '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>' ) ), NULL ) AS last_line_len, -- failure_error (error_type): identical expression/WHERE to the former -- failure_error CTE. if(ev.status = 'failure' AND ev.litellm_call_id != '', JSONExtractString(ev.calculated_payload, 'error_type'), NULL ) AS error_type FROM agent_events ev -- litellm_call_id (unique per call, confirmed) replaces the old -- m.timestamp = ev.timestamp equality join, which could silently pair a -- row with the wrong agent_messages row whenever two calls landed in the -- same millisecond (parallel subagent dispatch, MCP call bursts) - both -- tables now carry litellm_call_id in their ORDER BY for exactly this -- reason. Guarded by ev.litellm_call_id != '' so a row ingested before -- this column existed (permanently blank - see schema.sql's agent_events -- comment) simply fails to join rather than colliding with every other -- blank-call-id row in the same session. LEFT JOIN dedup_messages m ON m.session_id = ev.session_id AND ev.litellm_call_id != '' AND m.litellm_call_id = ev.litellm_call_id -- ExitPlanMode's own tool-call args don't carry the plan text (only an -- optional, now-deprecated freeform allowedPrompts field) - plan_proposals -- stores every plan text captured during the session, and there can be MORE -- plan_proposals rows than ExitPlanMode calls (intermediate revisions never -- submitted), so matching an ExitPlanMode row to "the plan it actually -- submitted" is a genuine ASOF heuristic (nearest-preceding captured_at), -- same pattern as child_anchor_raw above - not an exact link. Formerly its -- own plan_proposals_match CTE - merged directly in here, see this CTE's -- own leading comment above. ASOF LEFT JOIN plan_proposals pp ON pp.session_id = ev.session_id AND pp.captured_at <= ev.timestamp WHERE (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], ev.session_id)) ),usage_by_call AS ( SELECT u.session_id AS session_id, u.litellm_call_id AS litellm_call_id, sum((u.input_tokens - (1 - 1) * (u.cache_creation_tokens + u.cache_read_tokens)) + u.output_tokens) AS tok, sum(u.cost) AS cost FROM agent_usage u WHERE u.litellm_call_id != '' AND (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], u.session_id)) GROUP BY u.session_id, u.litellm_call_id ), -- A background subagent runs concurrently with the orchestrator's own -- continued work, so sorting every row purely by its own real timestamp -- interleaves two unrelated threads of activity (the subagent's steps and -- whatever the orchestrator did *while waiting*) into one jumbled stream. -- child_anchor gives every agent_invocation_id a single "anchor" timestamp -- - the orchestrator's own nearest-preceding Agent-spawn row - so the -- whole subagent block sorts as one contiguous unit right after its spawn -- point, instead of scattering across the orchestrator's concurrent rows. -- agent_invocations.parent_agent_id (populated at ingest from the caller's -- own x-claude-code-agent-id header) gives a real parent link for every row -- ingested after that column's rollout - NULL only on pre-migration/legacy -- rows, where this remains the same nearest-preceding ASOF heuristic as -- before (no real parent link exists for those - see agent_invocations' own -- comment in schema.sql), not one of the equality joins fixed by -- litellm_call_id above. agent_spawn_events AS ( SELECT ev.session_id AS session_id, ev.timestamp AS timestamp, ev.agent_invocation_id AS spawner_agent_id FROM agent_events ev WHERE ev.calculated_type = 'agent_spawn' AND (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], ev.session_id)) ), child_anchor_raw AS ( SELECT ai.session_id AS session_id, ai.agent_id AS agent_id, se.timestamp AS anchor_ts FROM agent_invocations ai ASOF LEFT JOIN agent_spawn_events se ON se.session_id = ai.session_id AND se.spawner_agent_id = coalesce(ai.parent_agent_id, '') AND ai.spawned_at >= se.timestamp WHERE (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], ai.session_id)) ), child_anchor AS ( -- agent_invocations can carry more than one row per agent_id (no FINAL -- applied to its ReplacingMergeTree here) - dedup to exactly one row per -- (session_id, agent_id) or the later join in the final SELECT would -- silently multiply every one of that subagent's event rows. SELECT session_id, agent_id, if(any(anchor_ts) = toDateTime64('1970-01-01 00:00:00', 3), NULL, any(anchor_ts)) AS anchor_ts FROM child_anchor_raw GROUP BY session_id, agent_id ), session_header AS ( SELECT ev.session_id AS session_id, any(ev.user_id) AS user_id, argMax(gb.git_branch, gb.captured_at) AS git_branch, argMax(gb.git_repo, gb.captured_at) AS git_repo, min(ev.timestamp) AS first_ts FROM agent_events ev LEFT JOIN session_git_branch gb ON gb.session_id = ev.session_id WHERE (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], ev.session_id)) GROUP BY ev.session_id ), stats_tokens AS ( SELECT u.session_id AS session_id, sum((u.input_tokens - (1 - 1) * (u.cache_creation_tokens + u.cache_read_tokens))) AS tok_in, sum(u.output_tokens) AS tok_out, sum(u.cost) AS cost_total, arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArray(u.model), ', ') AS models FROM agent_usage u WHERE u.model != '' AND (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], u.session_id)) GROUP BY u.session_id ), -- agent_events.agent_name is blank whenever the subagent's own rows raced -- ahead of the orchestrator's Agent tool_use/tool_result (best-effort lookup, -- see _agent_name_and_version_for_invocation's docstring in -- services/_common/src/ingest_db.py) - agent_invocations.subagent_type is the reliable -- source of "which subagents actually ran", so the two are unioned rather -- than trusting agent_events alone. agent_names_raw AS ( SELECT ev.session_id AS session_id, ev.agent_name AS name FROM agent_events ev WHERE ev.agent_name != '' AND (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], ev.session_id)) UNION ALL SELECT ai.session_id AS session_id, splitByChar('_', ai.subagent_type)[1] AS name FROM agent_invocations ai WHERE ai.subagent_type != '' AND splitByChar('_', ai.subagent_type)[1] != '' AND (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], ai.session_id)) ), stats_agent_names AS ( -- arrayFilter is defense-in-depth against any stray '' sneaking into the -- array (e.g. a future source added to the UNION above without its own -- empty-string guard) - arrayStringConcat would otherwise render it as a -- trailing ", " with nothing after it. SELECT session_id AS session_id, arrayStringConcat(arrayFilter(x -> x != '', groupUniqArray(name)), ', ') AS agents FROM agent_names_raw GROUP BY session_id ), stats_skills AS ( SELECT ev.session_id AS session_id, arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArrayIf(ev.skill_name, ev.skill_name != ''), ', ') AS skills FROM agent_events ev WHERE (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], ev.session_id)) GROUP BY ev.session_id ), stats_time AS ( SELECT ev.session_id AS session_id, dateDiff('second', min(ev.timestamp), max(ev.timestamp)) AS dur_sec, countIf(ev.tool_name != '') AS n_tools FROM agent_events ev WHERE (has([${session_id:singlequote}], '__all__') OR has([${session_id:singlequote}], ev.session_id)) GROUP BY ev.session_id ), -- prompt_calc/prompt_final are computed here (moved ahead of session_stats) so -- that stats_prompts below can reuse the same is_real classification used for -- the tie=2 marker glyph (❯ vs ○/●/🧐), instead of a separate, cruder "any row -- with prompt_text" count that lumps real user requests together with -- sys-checks/title-gen/suggestion-mode/judge calls. -- prompt_kind/display_text are read directly from calculated_payload, computed -- once at ingest by _prompt_kind_and_display in services/_common/src/ingest_parsing.py - a -- line-for-line port of this CTE pair's own former regex-based text-cleaning/ -- classification chain (system-reminder stripping, command-args extraction, -- interrupted-prefix stripping, summary/status tag extraction, whitespace/ -- blank-line collapsing, per-branch truncation). prompt_kind is deliberately -- NOT the same thing as calculated_type: calculated_type prioritizes "did this -- call's own response invoke a tool" over "what did the prompt that triggered -- it look like", so a system-notification/judge-call/etc prompt whose response -- happened to also call a tool used to get misclassified here as a real user -- prompt when this logic read is_sys/is_real off calculated_type. prompt_kind -- fixes that by always re-deriving the prompt's own shape from prompt_text, -- independently of calculated_type, exactly like the old regex chain did. prompt_calc AS ( SELECT sr.session_id, sr.timestamp AS ts, sr.litellm_call_id AS litellm_call_id, sr.agent_invocation_id AS agent_invocation_id, JSONExtractString(sr.calculated_payload, 'prompt_kind') AS prompt_kind, JSONExtractString(sr.calculated_payload, 'display_text') AS display_text, -- Bug fix (3rd "Prompts:" inflation bug): _prompt_kind_and_display (the -- ingest-side classifier, services/_common/src/ingest_parsing.py) runs an UNANCHORED -- regex search for ... ANYWHERE in the -- prompt text, before it ever checks whether the prompt is actually a -- -wrapped background severity check or a "this session is -- being continued from a previous conversation" compaction summary - -- both of which routinely echo an earlier /command invocation's own -- tag verbatim as part of the quoted history they carry. -- That misclassifies dozens of harness-internal re-sends per session as -- fresh prompt_kind='command' (i.e. is_real) rows, and each one has -- slightly different byte content (growing transcript/context), so the -- byte-exact first_prompt_occurrence_ts dedup above doesn't collapse -- them either - together these inflated one single /goal submission -- into ~17 counted "Prompts" in a real session. This is a genuine -- ingest-side classification bug (see this panel's own doc / AGENTS.md -- for the full writeup) - out of scope to fix in services/_common/src/ingest_parsing.py -- from here, but directly detectable and worth suppressing at query -- time: a GENUINE top-level /command invocation never itself contains -- a nested block or a "session is being continued" resume -- marker, so a 'command'-kind row containing either is, with no -- observed counterexample across multiple real sessions checked, a -- harness re-echo, not a new human command submission. (JSONExtractString(sr.calculated_payload, 'prompt_kind') = 'command' AND (position(sr.prompt_text, '') > 0 OR position(sr.prompt_text, 'This session is being continued from') > 0) ) AS is_command_echo, -- Bug fix: Claude Code's auto-compact resume turn re-injects the prior -- compact call's own summary as the very next "user"-role prompt, wrapped -- in a leading ... block (same wrapper -- tool_result_preview strips below) followed immediately by the literal -- "This session is being continued from a previous conversation..." -- marker text. This is harness-generated resumption context, not -- anything a human typed - but _prompt_kind_and_display has no dedicated -- branch for it (unlike the compact call's OWN response, which sets -- prompt_kind='compact'), so it falls through to prompt_kind='real' and -- used to render with the real-user ❯ marker plus the full raw summary -- text, dumping the whole compact recap into the trace as if the user -- had typed it. Confirmed live against session -- a28f342f-30d9-4a54-97da-ee289b016bd9 (61 prompt_kind='real' rows this -- session alone). Detected the same query-time-heuristic way as -- is_command_echo/is_tool_result_continuation/is_coordinator_message -- above: strip the leading system-reminder wrapper, then check the exact -- literal prefix Claude Code always uses for this resume message. startsWith( replaceRegexpOne(sr.prompt_text, '(?s)^(?:\s*.*?)+\s*', ''), 'This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context.' ) AS is_compact_resume, -- display_arg is the variable "gray argument" part of the line (severity -- score, agent-completion summary, ...), computed once at ingest by -- _prompt_kind_and_display alongside display_text - shown the same way -- tool_render shows a tool's own argument (a dimmed span after the fixed -- label/name), rather than being fused into display_text as plain-color -- text. Empty string for most prompt_kind rows (judge_call, title_gen, -- real user prompts, most system_notification branches, etc.), which -- render exactly as before with no added span. JSONExtractString(sr.calculated_payload, 'display_arg') AS display_arg, -- judge_ok/judge_reason: precomputed at ingest alongside prompt_kind for -- judge_call rows (the /goal judge's verdict and its free-text -- rationale). has_judge_ok distinguishes "key absent" (older -- un-reparsed rows, predating this field - show neither 👍 nor 👎) from -- an explicit false (JSONExtractBool alone can't tell these apart: it -- returns false for both a real `false` value and a missing key). JSONHas(sr.calculated_payload, 'judge_ok') AS has_judge_ok, JSONExtractBool(sr.calculated_payload, 'judge_ok') AS judge_ok, JSONExtractString(sr.calculated_payload, 'judge_reason') AS judge_reason, -- stop_hook_reason: precomputed at ingest for stop_hook_feedback rows (the -- model's own free-text assessment of whether the stop condition was -- met, extracted from the injected prompt itself via _STOP_HOOK_REASON_RE -- - see services/_common/src/ingest_parsing.py). Shown in full, unlike judge_reason, per -- this panel's own convention (no truncation cap for this field). JSONExtractString(sr.calculated_payload, 'stop_hook_reason') AS stop_hook_reason, (sr.agent_invocation_id != '' AND sr.rn_in_invocation = 1) AS is_agent_task, -- Bug fix: when the previous assistant turn called a tool, the Claude API -- puts that tool_result block into the NEXT request's "user" role. -- Claude Code sometimes appends a second content block alongside it (a -- bare system-reminder, a skill's own tool_result content rendered as a -- separate text block, etc.), so _last_user_text's own "all blocks are -- tool_result" skip (services/_common/src/ingest_parsing.py) doesn't catch it and -- prompt_text ends up literally "[tool_result]\n". -- This is never anything a human typed. -- None of _prompt_kind_and_display's prefix branches recognize this -- literal marker (it isn't a Claude Code lifecycle convention like -- system_notification/judge_call/etc.), so it falls through to -- prompt_kind='real' and used to render with the same real-user ❯ marker -- as a genuine prompt, get counted in "Prompts:", and (worse, on a -- session's very first row) get picked as the session's first_real start -- marker. -- Detected here the same way is_command_echo is (a query-time heuristic -- on the raw prompt_text, not an ingest-side reclassification) since -- this is a display-time distinction, not a new calculated_type. startsWith(sr.prompt_text, '[tool_result]') AS is_tool_result_continuation, -- Bug fix: a resumed background subagent's next turn can be fed a -- relayed message FROM THE ORCHESTRATOR (SendMessage-style "the -- coordinator sent a message while you were working" injections), not -- anything the actual human typed. Confirmed against real -- agent_messages rows - the literal prefix is exact/stable (no trailing- -- space or colon variance observed across multiple sessions), always at -- position 0 of the raw prompt_text (never behind a stripped -- system-reminder first). Same query-time-heuristic pattern as -- is_command_echo/is_tool_result_continuation above - this isn't a -- Claude Code lifecycle convention _prompt_kind_and_display already -- recognizes, so it falls through to prompt_kind='real' and, left -- unchecked, renders with the real-user ❯ marker and counts toward -- "Prompts:"/first_real just like a genuine human message would. startsWith(sr.prompt_text, 'The coordinator sent a message while you were working:') AS is_coordinator_message, -- Best-effort preview of whatever text WAS attached alongside the -- tool_result block (so the row isn't just a bare, uninformative label): -- strip the literal "[tool_result]" marker, then strip a leading -- system-reminder wrapper if that's what follows (same tag this panel's -- own doc already documents stripping elsewhere, just re-anchored here -- since it may not sit at position 0 of the raw prompt_text - only of -- what's left after the marker), collapse whitespace runs (this whole -- panel renders inside a 
), then cap to a short preview length.
    -- Same 120-char convention already used for judge_reason/collaboration-
    -- mode/AskUserQuestion's nested grey lines.
    -- Collapsing whitespace BEFORE trimBoth (not after) matters: trimBoth
    -- only strips literal spaces, not newlines/tabs, so trimming first left
    -- a stray leading "\n" that the later whitespace-collapse turned into a
    -- visible leading space.

      trimBoth(
        replaceRegexpAll(
          replaceRegexpOne(
            replaceOne(sr.prompt_text, '[tool_result]', ''),
            '(?s)^(?:\s*.*?)+\s*', ''
          ),
          '[ \t\n\r]+', ' '

      1, 120
    ) AS tool_result_preview

  -- own comment above): prompt_kind='command' rows dedup on the clean

  -- prompt_text, since Codex's own self-resends of the same command carry a
  -- changing token-budget counter inside the raw text that defeats
  -- byte-exact dedup. Every other prompt_kind keeps the original byte-exact
  -- first_prompt_occurrence_ts dedup unchanged - those don't have this
  -- changing-counter problem, so there's no reason to loosen their dedup key.

    JSONExtractString(sr.calculated_payload, 'prompt_kind') = 'command',

),
prompt_final AS (
  SELECT session_id, ts, litellm_call_id, agent_invocation_id, is_agent_task,
    has_judge_ok, judge_ok, judge_reason, stop_hook_reason,
    prompt_kind = 'webpage_content' AS is_webpage,
    prompt_kind = 'suggestion_mode' AS is_sugg,
    prompt_kind = 'judge_call' AS is_judge,
    prompt_kind = 'stop_hook_feedback' AS is_stop_hook,
    prompt_kind = 'title_gen' AS is_title,
    -- 'compact' marks Claude Code's auto-compact context-summarization
    -- call - an internal, never-user-typed LLM call whose response opens
    -- with ... then .... Ingest
    -- (_prompt_kind_and_display) always sets display_text to the literal
    -- '/compact' and display_arg to the analysis-stripped summary excerpt
    -- (~100 words, already truncated at ingest). Like transcript_handoff/
    -- judge_call/system_notification, this is background/system-triggered,
    -- not real user input - deliberately NOT added to the is_real allowlist
    -- below, so it falls through to the same muted '○' marker every other
    -- background kind gets.
    prompt_kind = 'compact' AS is_compact,
    -- ALLOWLIST (flipped from a denylist after 'away_recap' silently defaulted
    -- to real-user ❯ styling on arrival - a denylist means every future
    -- prompt_kind is real-user by default unless someone remembers to add it
    -- to an exclusion list, which is exactly what just happened). Only 'real'
    -- (a genuine freeform user prompt) and 'command' (an actual slash-command
    -- invocation) are user-authored input, PLUS 'interrupted' (a
    -- '[Request interrupted by user]'-prefixed prompt still carries real
    -- user-authored text once the prefix is stripped - see
    -- _prompt_kind_and_display's own docstring/branch - so it's genuine user
    -- input, not harness noise, despite the special prefix). Every other
    -- prompt_kind (system_notification, suggestion_mode, judge_call, title_gen,
    -- transcript_handoff, stop_hook_feedback, away_recap, webpage_content, and
    -- any future kind) now falls through to the muted ○ marker by default, with
    -- zero further list-maintenance required. webpage_content is deliberately
    -- NOT in this allowlist (it's tool output echoed back as a 'user'-role
    -- turn, not user-authored text) - this changes nothing visible since
    -- is_webpage already overrides the marker to ● ahead of is_real in the
    -- render chain below, and stats_prompts already excludes is_webpage rows
    -- from the count too.
    -- AND NOT is_command_echo: see is_command_echo's own comment above -
    -- excludes 'command'-kind rows that are actually a harness re-echo of an
    -- earlier command's own  tag (a -wrapped
    -- severity check, or a "session is being continued" compaction summary),
    -- not a fresh human command submission.
    -- AND NOT is_tool_result_continuation: see is_tool_result_continuation's
    -- own comment above - a "[tool_result]"-prefixed prompt_text is an
    -- automatic API continuation (the previous turn's tool result, plus
    -- whatever Claude Code attached alongside it), never anything a human
    -- typed, regardless of which prompt_kind it happened to fall into.
    -- AND NOT is_coordinator_message: see is_coordinator_message's own
    -- comment above - a relayed orchestrator message fed into a resumed
    -- background subagent's next turn, never anything a human typed either.
    (prompt_kind IN ('real', 'command', 'interrupted') AND NOT is_command_echo AND NOT is_tool_result_continuation AND NOT is_coordinator_message AND NOT is_compact_resume) AS is_real,
    is_command_echo,
    is_tool_result_continuation,
    is_coordinator_message,
    is_compact_resume,
    if(is_tool_result_continuation,
      concat('[background] tool result continuation', if(tool_result_preview != '', concat(': ', tool_result_preview), '')),
      if(is_command_echo, '[background] resent context (harness echo of an earlier command)',
        if(is_compact_resume, '[background] compact-resume context (auto-injected conversation summary)', display_text)
      )
    ) AS display,
    -- display_arg, HTML-escaped the same way tool_render escapes its own
    -- raw_args -> escaped_args (a 90-char safety cap, then '&'/'<'/'>' only -
    -- no markdown/newline handling, since these values are short single-line
    -- facts like "2/100" or an agent-completion summary, not free-form
    -- prompt/reply text). Deliberately left at 90 (NOT bumped alongside
    -- tool_render's raw_args -> 110): this field renders on the tie=2
    -- prompt-marker line, which never appends the duration/tokens/cost
    -- stats column, so it isn't part of the single-line/last-line
    -- padding-before-stats system these two caps otherwise share elsewhere.
    -- Reused verbatim below inside the exact same
    -- ... gray-argument markup tool_render
    -- already wraps its own escaped_args in, so these rows visually match
    -- tool-call rows: label/name in normal color, then a gray span for the
    -- variable part. Empty when display_arg is empty (the common case), so
    -- the row-rendering branch below can cheaply check != ''. Replaces the
    -- former tooltip_attr mechanism (a hover-only title="" attribute for
    -- transcript_handoff's severity-check verdict) - now redundant since
    -- display_arg already carries that same "block: yes/no" info as visible
    -- gray text.
    -- 'compact' rows carry a ~100-word summary excerpt in display_arg,
    -- already truncated at ingest - unlike every other prompt_kind's short
    -- single-line display_arg (severity score, agent summary, ...), this
    -- one is deliberately NOT re-capped to the shared 90-char safety cap
    -- below, or the excerpt would be chopped down to a handful of words.
    replaceAll(replaceAll(replaceAll(
      if(prompt_kind = 'compact', display_arg, substringUTF8(display_arg, 1, 90)),
      '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>') AS display_arg_escaped
  FROM prompt_calc
),
stats_prompts AS (
  -- Only count genuine user-authored requests (the same is_real flag that
  -- drives the ❯ marker glyph below), excluding is_webpage (which overrides
  -- is_real's marker to ● even though is_real can be true for it) - anything
  -- else (sys-checks, title-gen, suggestion-mode, judge calls, transcript
  -- handoffs) is harness noise, not something the user asked for, and must
  -- not be lumped into "Prompts:". is_agent_task (a subagent's own spawn
  -- task, echoed back as its first "user"-role turn - see is_agent_task's
  -- own comment above) is likewise not user-authored and excluded here too.
  SELECT session_id AS session_id, countIf(is_real AND NOT is_webpage AND NOT is_agent_task) AS n_prompts
  FROM prompt_final
  GROUP BY session_id
),
session_stats AS (
  SELECT st.session_id AS session_id,
    concat(
      'StartedAt: ', formatDateTime(toTimeZone(sh.first_ts, 'UTC'), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%S'), '
',
      'Duration: ', if(st.dur_sec >= 86400, concat(toString(intDiv(st.dur_sec, 86400)), 'd ', toString(intDiv(st.dur_sec % 86400, 3600)), 'h'), if(st.dur_sec >= 3600, concat(toString(intDiv(st.dur_sec, 3600)), 'h ', toString(intDiv(st.dur_sec % 3600, 60)), 'm'), if(st.dur_sec >= 60, concat(toString(intDiv(st.dur_sec, 60)), 'm ', toString(st.dur_sec % 60), 's'), concat(toString(st.dur_sec), 's')))), '\n',
      'Cost: $', toString(round(coalesce(sk.cost_total, 0), 2)), '\n',
      'Tokens: ', multiIf(coalesce(sk.tok_in, 0) >= 1000000, concat(toString(round(coalesce(sk.tok_in, 0) / 1000000., 1)), 'm'), coalesce(sk.tok_in, 0) >= 1000, concat(toString(round(coalesce(sk.tok_in, 0) / 1000., 1)), 'k'), toString(coalesce(sk.tok_in, 0))), ' in / ', multiIf(coalesce(sk.tok_out, 0) >= 1000000, concat(toString(round(coalesce(sk.tok_out, 0) / 1000000., 1)), 'm'), coalesce(sk.tok_out, 0) >= 1000, concat(toString(round(coalesce(sk.tok_out, 0) / 1000., 1)), 'k'), toString(coalesce(sk.tok_out, 0))), ' out\n',
      'Model(s): ', coalesce(sk.models, ''), '\n',
      'Prompts: ', toString(coalesce(pr.n_prompts, 0)), '\n',
      'Tool calls: ', toString(st.n_tools), '\n',
      'Agents: ', if(coalesce(an.agents, '') = '', 'none', an.agents), '\n',
      'Skills: ', if(coalesce(sl.skills, '') = '', 'none', sl.skills), '\n',
      'Git: ', if(coalesce(sh.git_repo, '') = '' AND coalesce(sh.git_branch, '') = '', 'unknown', concat(if(sh.git_repo != '', sh.git_repo, '?'), ':', if(sh.git_branch != '', sh.git_branch, '?')))
    ) AS block
  FROM stats_time st
  LEFT JOIN stats_tokens sk ON sk.session_id = st.session_id
  LEFT JOIN stats_agent_names an ON an.session_id = st.session_id
  LEFT JOIN stats_skills sl ON sl.session_id = st.session_id
  LEFT JOIN stats_prompts pr ON pr.session_id = st.session_id
  LEFT JOIN session_header sh ON sh.session_id = st.session_id
),
tie2_ts AS (
  -- Every (session_id, litellm_call_id) that actually renders a tie=2
  -- prompt-marker line (i.e. survives that branch's own is_title/is_sugg
  -- filter) - used so the tie=3 branch (reply, and Agent-spawn/failure
  -- rows) can tell whether a visible timestamp was already shown on the
  -- marker line immediately above it in the tree (same underlying call),
  -- and suppress its own otherwise-duplicate timestamp rather than
  -- stacking two identical HH:MM:SS values on adjacent lines.
  SELECT DISTINCT pf.session_id AS session_id, pf.litellm_call_id AS litellm_call_id
  FROM prompt_final pf
  WHERE NOT pf.is_title AND NOT pf.is_sugg
),
first_real AS (
  -- Anything before the session's first genuine (non-harness) user message is
  -- pre-conversation noise (a silent auto-retry, a warm-up ping) invisible in
  -- the CLI itself - drop it rather than showing a confusing orphan FAIL row.
  -- Bug fix: is_real alone isn't enough here - a newly-spawned subagent's own
  -- first "user"-role turn (is_agent_task, the orchestrator's own task/prompt
  -- echoed back, not anything a human typed) still satisfies is_real's own
  -- prompt_kind check, so without this extra exclusion first_real's min(ts)
  -- could land on a background subagent's spawn-task timestamp instead of the
  -- session's actual first human message - reproduced live: the tree started
  -- mid-conversation at an assistant reply with no visible timestamp, because
  -- fr.ts had been pulled back to a subagent task-echo row that predated the
  -- real conversation. is_agent_task rows already render with their own '●'
  -- marker regardless (see is_agent_task's own comment above) - this only
  -- keeps them from ALSO acting as the session's start-of-trace cutoff.
  SELECT session_id, min(ts) AS ts
  FROM prompt_final
  WHERE is_real AND NOT is_agent_task
  GROUP BY session_id
)
SELECT session_id,
  arrayStringConcat(
    arrayMap(x -> x.4, arraySort(x -> (x.1, x.2, x.3), groupArray((sort_ts, tie, ts, line)))),
    '\n'
  ) AS tree
FROM (
  SELECT session_id, first_ts AS ts, first_ts AS sort_ts, 0 AS tie,
    concat('') AS line
  FROM session_header

  UNION ALL

  SELECT ss.session_id, sh.first_ts AS ts, sh.first_ts AS sort_ts, 1 AS tie,
    concat('\n', ss.block, '\n\n') AS line
  FROM session_stats ss
  INNER JOIN session_header sh ON sh.session_id = ss.session_id

  UNION ALL

  -- MERGED (candidate2 rewrite): the three UNION ALL branches that each
  -- independently re-scanned prompt_final/first_real/child_anchor (tie=2 main
  -- marker, tie=4 judge_reason, tie=4 stop_hook_reason) are collapsed into a
  -- single pass over prompt_final, since ClickHouse re-executes a WITH-CTE on
  -- every textual reference. Each branch's own predicate is now evaluated
  -- per-row into a (tie, line) tuple array; arrayFilter drops the branches
  -- that don't apply to that row (tie=0. sentinel), and ARRAY JOIN expands
  -- whichever of the (up to 3) tuples survive back into individual result
  -- rows - reproducing the exact same "zero, one, two, or three output rows
  -- per prompt_final row" semantics the three separate UNION ALL branches had
  -- (e.g. a judge_call row independently emits both its own tie=2 marker AND
  -- its tie=4 judge_reason line - these are not mutually exclusive
  -- alternatives, so a plain multiIf/CASE picking ONE variant per row would
  -- be wrong; the array+ARRAY JOIN preserves the union's multi-row-per-input
  -- behavior). All three branches share the identical
  -- FROM prompt_final pf INNER JOIN first_real fr LEFT JOIN child_anchor ca
  -- shape, so prompt_final now costs 1x here instead of 3x.
  SELECT pf.session_id, pf.ts, if(pf.agent_invocation_id != '', coalesce(ca.anchor_ts, pf.ts), pf.ts) AS sort_ts, trow.1 AS tie, trow.2 AS line
  FROM prompt_final pf
  INNER JOIN first_real fr ON fr.session_id = pf.session_id
  LEFT JOIN child_anchor ca ON ca.session_id = pf.session_id AND ca.agent_id = pf.agent_invocation_id
  ARRAY JOIN arrayFilter(t -> t.1 != 0., [
    if(NOT pf.is_title AND NOT pf.is_sugg, (2., concat(
      -- The visible HH:MM:SS is just link text - the href carries this
      -- call's litellm_call_id (unique per call, confirmed) so the detail
      -- table below can match the exact agent_events row, replacing the
      -- old toString(pf.ts) value: two different rows sharing the same
      -- millisecond (parallel subagent dispatch, MCP bursts) would
      -- otherwise be ambiguous from a timestamp string alone, which
      -- litellm_call_id cannot be. A plain href replaces the *entire*
      -- query string on click (not just adds to it) - onclick+
      -- URLSearchParams.set() would merge instead, but Grafana's own HTML
      -- sanitizer (textUtil.sanitize(), on by default - see
      -- disableSanitizeHtml in grafana.ini) strips inline event handlers
      -- like onclick from Text-panel HTML, so that approach silently does
      -- nothing on click. Explicitly re-stating var-session_id (this row's
      -- own session, not whatever else was selected) alongside
      -- var-trace_ts keeps the session correct; the time range and active
      -- tab aren't preserved this way, but this panel's own query never
      -- filters by time range anyway.
      '', formatDateTime(toTimeZone(pf.ts, 'UTC'), '%H:%i:%S'), '', '  ',
      -- is_agent_task: a subagent's own spawn task, echoed back as its
      -- first "user"-role turn (see is_agent_task's own comment above) -
      -- authored by the orchestrator's model, not typed by a human. Unlike
      -- every other marker in this branch, is_agent_task ALWAYS renders as
      -- a bare bullet with no indent and no tree connector (└─/├─),
      -- regardless of whether the echoed task text is present or
      -- empty/blank - this row is never nested visually under anything,
      -- so an indent+connector prefix here would misleadingly imply
      -- parentage that doesn't exist for this node.
      if(pf.is_agent_task,
        '● ',
        concat(
          if(pf.agent_invocation_id != '', '   ', ''),
          -- judge_call now shares the same hollow-circle ○ marker used for
          -- every other background/harness row (system_notification,
          -- transcript_handoff, ...) - it used to get its own 🧐 emoji, but
          -- the verdict itself is now surfaced via a 👍/👎 to the right of
          -- the row instead (see below), so a distinct marker glyph is no
          -- longer needed here.
          if(pf.is_webpage, '● ', if(pf.is_real, '❯ ', '○ '))
        )
      ),
      -- Render display_text (normal color, with the usual markdown/newline/
      -- slash-command conversions) as before, then append display_arg_escaped
      -- (when non-empty) wrapped in the SAME gray-span markup tool_render
      -- already uses for its own args after a tool name
      -- (...) - visually unifying these rows
      -- with tool-call rows: label/name, then a gray span for the variable
      -- part. When display_arg_escaped is empty (the common case for most
      -- prompt_kind rows), this renders exactly as before with no added span.
